summary: Lets an LDAP client read the target entry of an update before and/or after the change is applied. The reads happen atomically as part of the update. It is a proposed standard.

plainLanguage.summary: Take a snapshot of a page before and after you edit it, in one step so nobody can sneak in between.

subtitle: Ask the directory server to hand back a copy of an entry from just before or just after your update, in the same atomic step.

tldr.problem: After an LDAP client changes an entry, it may need the old values that were replaced, or server-set values such as entryUUID and modifyTimestamp. Reading them in a separate request leaves a gap in which other updates can slip in.
tldr.mechanism: The Pre-Read and Post-Read request controls ask the server to return a copy of the target entry before or after the update. The copy comes back in a matching response control, and the read is processed atomically with the update.
tldr.outcome: A client can capture deleted or replaced values, or server-maintained operational attributes, as part of one update. The controls are a Proposed Standard modeled on similar X.500 DAP capabilities.

today: RFC 4527 is a Proposed Standard, and the unit metadata shows no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It was published in June 2006 together with the related assertion control in RFC 4528.

sections.title: Reading the Entry You Are Updating
sections.content:
RFC 4527 extends the Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) so a client can read the target entry of an update operation such as Add, Delete, Modify or ModifyDN. It does this with controls, extra pieces that a client attaches to a request to change how the server handles it.

There are two request controls. The Pre-Read control asks for a copy of the entry before the update is applied. The Post-Read control asks for a copy after it is applied. Each request control has a corresponding response control that carries the entry back.

The RFC gives two uses. Pre-Read can obtain replaced or deleted values of modified attributes, or a copy of the entry being deleted. Post-Read can obtain values of operational attributes the server updates as part of the operation, such as entryUUID and modifyTimestamp. The functionality is based on similar functionality in the X.500 Directory Access Protocol (DAP).
sections.plainLanguage: Normally when you change a page in a notebook, you cannot see what it said before. These controls let you ask the notebook keeper for a copy of the page from before or after your change.

sections.title: The Pre-Read Controls
sections.content:
The Pre-Read request and response controls are identified by the object identifier 1.3.6.1.1.13.1. Servers that implement them SHOULD publish that identifier as a value of supportedControl in their root DSE (the server's own description entry).

The request control carries a BER-encoded AttributeSelection, as extended by RFC 3673, which says which attributes should appear in the copy. Its criticality may be TRUE or FALSE. It is appropriate for modifyRequest, delRequest and modDNRequest messages.

The response control holds, in an OCTET STRING, a BER-encoded SearchResultEntry with the values of the requested attributes, subject to access controls and other constraints. It is appropriate for the matching responses with a resultCode of success (0). If the update fails, in either normal or control processing, no Pre-Read response control is provided.
sections.plainLanguage: Before the server changes or removes something, it takes a snapshot of the parts you asked about and hands it back to you afterwards.

sections.title: The Post-Read Controls
sections.content:
The Post-Read controls work the same way but are identified by 1.3.6.1.1.13.2. They ask for a copy of the target entry after the update has been applied. Servers implementing them SHOULD publish that identifier in supportedControl in their root DSE.

The request control is appropriate for addRequest, modifyRequest and modDNRequest, and its value is a BER-encoded AttributeSelection. The response control carries a BER-encoded SearchResultEntry and is appropriate for the matching responses with a resultCode of success (0).

As with Pre-Read, the returned attributes are subject to access controls and other constraints, and if the update fails no Post-Read response control is provided.

Pre-Read applies to Modify, Delete and ModifyDN. Post-Read applies to Add, Modify and ModifyDN. An Add has no earlier entry to read, and a Delete has no later one.
sections.plainLanguage: The same idea, but the snapshot is taken after your change, so you can see exactly what the finished page looks like, including things the server wrote itself.

sections.title: Atomicity and Other Controls
sections.content:
For both controls, the normal processing of the update operation and the processing of the control MUST be performed as one atomic action isolated from other update operations. This is what gives the client a trustworthy before or after picture: no other update can land in between.

The Pre-Read and Post-Read controls may be combined with each other and with other controls. When combined with the assertion control (RFC 4528) or the manageDsaIT control (RFC 3296), the semantics of each control in the combination applies. Other combinations may be detailed in other specifications.
sections.plainLanguage: The before and after photos are taken in the same instant as the change, so nobody can sneak in between. You can also mix these controls with others.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
These controls extend update operations with read capability, so two permissions matter. Servers MUST ensure that the client is authorized to read the information the control provides, and that the client is authorized to perform the requested directory update.

The security considerations for the update operations in RFC 4511, and the general LDAP considerations in RFC 4510, also apply.
sections.plainLanguage: Being allowed to edit a page does not automatically mean you may read everything on it. The server checks both permissions.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: IANA registered an LDAP object identifier to identify the protocol elements defined in this document. It also registered two LDAP protocol mechanisms, both with usage Control: 1.3.6.1.1.13.1 for the LDAP Pre-read Control and 1.3.6.1.1.13.2 for the LDAP Post-read Control. The change controller is the IESG.
sections.plainLanguage: The two controls got official numbers in a public list, so everyone uses the same numbers for the same thing.
